instructions.content: NEVER skip the build check before pushing -- a broken build blocks the deployment CI job and requires a separate fix commit, wasting time and polluting git history.
NEVER leave orphan pages unlinked -- orphan pages are invisible to navigation and search, wasting the effort spent writing them.
NEVER add an ADR without updating docs/ADR/index.yaml in the same commit -- the index is the canonical discovery mechanism; a missing entry means the ADR may as well not exist.
NEVER reference a page that does not exist -- broken links degrade trust in the documentation and produce 404s for visitors.
Build first, ask questions later -- always start with the build check, it is the fastest path to failure and catches mechanical issues early.
Fix the source, not the output -- when a check reveals a problem, fix the markdown source, not the built site/ directory, since the build is ephemeral.
Escalate to the right skill -- redirect content quality issues to markdown-authoring, and skill documentation concerns to skill-quality-auditor.
Automate what you check twice -- if the same issue is caught twice, add a script or CI step so it is never checked manually again.
After a successful build, confirm the page count is reasonable (typically 45-55 pages for this project) -- a sudden drop signals missing content.
Reconcile on-disk ADRs with docs/ADR/index.yaml in both directions -- unregistered ADRs need adding, and stale index entries referencing deleted files need removing.
When llms.enabled is true in docmd.config.json, verify llms.txt, llms-full.txt, and llms.json exist in the build output and contain non-zero entries.
Adapt to the situation -- unless the CI deployment is already broken, the build check may be skipped for trivial doc tweaks (single-word fixes, typo corrections).
The workflow order is: build check, orphan detection, ADR index freshness, LLM output audit, preview, then commit and push.
